newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Britain well-regarded by one-third of Argentines.
newsitem.headline: Britain well-regarded by one-third of Argentines.

text.p: A third of Argentines have a positive image of their former Falklands War foe Britain, a quarter take a negative view and another quarter are indifferent, according to an opinion poll released on Monday.

A poll of 780 Buenos Aires residents by a private think-tank, the Centre of Studies Union for the New Majority, showed 32 percent had a good impression of Britain, 25 percent had a bad impression and 24 percent took a "regular" view.
The survey was carried out last month, ahead of historic visits to Britain this week by Argentina's army chief and a major trade mission.
General Martin Balza, who commanded an artillery unit in the 10-week South Atlantic war in 1982, on Monday became the first Argentine army head to visit Britain since the war.
Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez landed in London on Monday with 100 business leaders.

About 1,000 servicemen died in the war after Britain sent a task force to dislodge Argentine troops from the Falklands. Argentina still claims the islands, which it calls the Malvinas, but the two countries have renewed diplomatic links.
